title: Basic Calculator
description:
Given a string `s` representing a valid mathematical expression, implement a basic calculator to evaluate it, and return the result of the evaluation.

The expression string contains only non-negative integers, `'+'`, `'-'`, `'('`, `')'`, and space characters `' '`.

Note that:
- `'+'` is not used as a unary operation (for example, `"+1"` and `"+(2 + 3)"` are invalid).
- `'-'` may be used as a unary operation (for example, `"-1"` and `"-(2 + 3)"` are valid).
- There will be no two consecutive operators in the input.
- Every number and running calculation will fit in a signed 32-bit integer.
- Do not use any built-in expression evaluator such as `eval()`.
constraints: '+' is not used as a unary operation, while '-' may be used as a unary operation.
There will be no two consecutive operators in the input.
Every number and running calculation will fit in a signed 32-bit integer.
hints: Without parentheses, you can evaluate the expression in one left-to-right pass by maintaining a running total and the current sign (+1 or -1).
When you encounter '(', save the current running total and sign onto a stack, then reset both to evaluate the sub-expression inside the parentheses.
When you encounter ')', finish the current number, multiply the sub-expression's result by the saved sign, and add it back to the saved running total.
